title: Cerro Armazones at night
caption: A fish-eye view of the night sky at Cerro Armazones, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at the ELT site, Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This fish-eye view takes in the night sky above ESO's Astronomical Site Monitor on Cerro Armazones, a mountain in the Chilean desert near Paranal Observatory, where the Very Large Telescope (VLT) is based. A fish-eye lens squeezes an extremely wide field of view into a single frame.

Instruments like a site monitor are used to keep track of observing conditions at a location. Choosing where to put a major telescope depends on this kind of measurement, and Cerro Armazones was ultimately picked to host the planned European Extremely Large Telescope (E-ELT).

With a mirror in the 40-meter class, the E-ELT was expected to become the world's biggest eye on the sky. The quiet mountaintop in this picture was chosen to be its home, close to its neighbor the VLT at Paranal.

understand.eye: A fish-eye lens takes in far more of the sky at once than the eye can, bending the view into one frame.
